comparison: Perfect agreement on in vivo validation claims (C39-C42, C76-C77). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical analysis while acknowledging missing normality test details. Peer reviewers accept findings without criticism and emphasize significance for immune response research.

Both address speculative/therapeutic claims (C59-C60, C63-C64). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable hypotheses requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED but implicitly acknowledge these as speculative extensions rather than direct experimental findings, accepting broader implications without challenge.

Strong agreement on co-culture system claims (C32-C37). Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes physiological relevance and consistency with proposed mechanism. Peer reviewers accept findings as demonstrating gradient formation ability in detail, considering it useful work without raising concerns.

Agreement on main conclusions (C54-C56, C61-C62, C68, C81). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple lines of evidence supporting the mechanistic model. Peer reviewers affirm this as solid evidence and a useful advance contributing to understanding of GAG roles in gradient creation.

Agreement on HS-dependent phase separation and chemotaxis claims (C26-C31). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights comprehensive convergence across CHO cell comparisons, competitive inhibition, and mutant studies. Peer reviewers accept cell-based findings and value the work for understanding GAG roles in leukocyte migration.

Strong agreement on core LLPS evidence (C3-C10). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging experimental evidence from multiple techniques and consistency with electrostatic interaction mechanism. Peer reviewers provide solid endorsement without critique. Peer R1 also includes BBXB motif claims (C12-C14) that OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

Agreement on gradient formation via phase separation (C15-C18). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes differential behavior between heparin-beads and Ni-NTA beads demonstrating importance of immobilization mode. Peer reviewers accept as solid evidence for functional importance. Peer R2 also includes chemotaxis claims (C19-C21) that OpenEval addresses separately in R4.

Agreement on functional chemotaxis claims (C19-C21). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights dramatic differences between bead types and mutant behavior as strong evidence for phase separation-mediated mechanism. Peer reviewers accept these findings as demonstrating functional importance without raising concerns about bead-based assay.

Agreement on cell surface phase separation (C22-C25). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes clear differential behavior between CHO-K1 and CHO-677 cells demonstrating HS dependence with liquid-like FRAP properties. Peer reviewers accept without criticism as part of valuable work on GAG effects on leukocyte migration.

Agreement on BBXB motif importance (C11-C14, C52-C53). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistency between mutant experimental data and computational predictions. Peer R1 includes these claims (C12-C14) alongside core LLPS evidence, accepting the mutant analysis and docking results without critique.

Agreement on background/contextual claims (C1-C2, C43-C46, C69-C72). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these represent appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge foundational context about chemokines creating gradients via GAG binding as accepted understanding.

Divergence on oligomerization-LLPS relationship (C49, C65-C67). OpenEval R12 rates background claims as SUPPORTED without flagging concerns. Peer R7 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting LLPS not detected at lower CCL5 concentrations and requesting clarification in discussion about whether oligomerization is crucial for LLPS.

Both address mechanistic interpretation claims (C78-C79). OpenEval R1 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation of LLPS mechanism with weak electrostatic interactions. Peer R9 also rates as SUPPORTED, accepting mechanistic framework without critique as part of broader acceptance of phase separation evidence.

Agreement on mechanistic comparison claims (C47-C48, C73). OpenEval R12 includes these as SUPPORTED background/contextual claims. Peer R9 accepts mechanistic framework as SUPPORTED without challenge, focusing instead on oligomerization-LLPS relationship clarification needs.

Both address primary blood cell claims (C38). OpenEval R8 rates as SUPPORTED, noting physiological relevance while acknowledging high variability between samples. Peer R4 includes C38 in broader acceptance of co-culture findings as SUPPORTED without specific concerns about primary cell variability.
